title: Slew-rate prefill redistributor for latency-aware fairness and kernel hinting
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th percentile decode latency for multi-tenant hosted API without worsening throughput or adding manual operator load.

Background: Current prefill/decode arbitration occasionally lets short low-priority decodes and long prefill-heavy requests contend, producing latency tail spikes. Kernel selection hints exist at RPC boundary but are not integrated with tenant-level rate shaping. We propose a 'slew-rate redistributor' that smooths incoming prefill admission per-tenant, dynamically staggers phase splits, and emits kernel hinting metadata to downstream router for opportunistic demotion.

Design summary:
- Tenant slewing: track short-window token ingress rate per tenant and compute a configurable 'slew' budget. New prefill requests for a tenant consume budget; when budget exhausted we softly delay admission by micro-sleeps (adjusted by SLA class).
- Phase staggerer: for admitted prefill requests, allow the prefill stage to be split into micro-phases (N=2..6) using attention-density heuristics computed from prompt stats; interleave decode/streamable-gen to reduce resource lock contention.
- Kernel hinting: attach lightweight kernel preference tags (e.g., 'fast-attn', 'quantized-heavy', 'kv-shared-friendly') based on prompt length/attn-density so router can steer to compatible kernels or demote to cheaper kernels during congestion.
- Fairness policy: combine proportional share based on committed capacity with slew backpressure to prevent starvation; tenants with high SLA can be allowed higher burst factor.

Measurement plan:
- Benchmarks: end-to-end 95p and 99p latency, throughput (tokens/sec), per-tenant token cost delta, and kernel-selection distribution.
- Testbeds: internal perf cluster v3 and canary on dedicated pool with synthetic mixes and production trace replay (Week 1: offline; Week 2: canary 5% traffic).

Rollout:
- Feature flag gated per-tenant with default off. Start with low-risk tenants and internal staging apps. Observe tail latency and error rates for 3 days before expanding.

Open questions:
- Optimal micro-sleep sizing and jittering parameters.
- Interactions with existing prefill-decode hedging and admission controllers (ENG-271828).
- Safety of kernel demotion for model correctness and quantization regressions.
